title: Pullable streaming adapter: cancellable AsyncGenerator recipes and retry semantics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Users integrating Redwood TS SDK into browser and server runtimes struggle to express pull-based consumption patterns with clear cancellation, deterministic backpressure, and predictable retry semantics. Existing docs show either raw ReadableStream usage (browser-only) or AsyncIterable patterns (node-centric) but not a small, composable adapter that lets both runtimes interoperate with cancellation and retry behaviours preserved.

Goal: Implement and document a 'pullable' streaming adapter that bridges Web ReadableStream, AsyncGenerator/AsyncIterable, and the SDK streaming primitives. Provide ergonomic, tested recipes that: 1) support explicit cancellation (from consumer or producer), 2) surface partial results while preserving retry boundaries, and 3) minimize memory retention by honoring backpressure. Ship implementation + tests + example recipes in the SDK repo and a short Console/Docs how-to.
acceptance_criteria: A TypeScript adapter utility (pullableStreamAdapter) exists and is exported from @redwood/sdk-streams with typings.
Adapter interops with: ReadableStream (browser), AsyncIterable/AsyncGenerator (node), and the SDK streaming response object without bespoke user glue.
Cancellation initiated by consumer cancels underlying fetch/connection and releases KV cache references; no unbounded Promise leaks observed in stress tests.

Retryable error semantics documented: transient network errors cause controlled, idempotent retries up to configured attempts; partial chunks are either resumed or invalidated according to recipe choices.
Example recipes added to docs/recipes/streaming with both browser and Node usage and at least two real-world patterns (live-chat UI, long-polling single-request rerank + stream).
Integration tests cover race conditions: simultaneous consumer cancel + producer push, adapter error propagation, and backpressure stress under concurrency load.
tasks: Design adapter API surface and TS typings (pair with SDK typings owners).
Implement base adapter bridging ReadableStream <-> AsyncGenerator (handles chunk framing and backpressure).
Add cancellation signaling that wires through AbortController to underlying request/connection.
Implement retry wrapper with idempotency token support and configurable backoff for transient failures.
Write unit tests for adapter plumbing and edge cases (double-cancel, slow consumer, producer burst).
Add end-to-end examples: browser chat component with ReadableStream consumption, Node CLI consumer using for-await-of, and a server-side rerank stream scenario.
Docs: short guide, recipe snippets, and migration notes for existing customers.
Create a small benchmark script to measure memory and latency under expected workloads and compare with current adapter baseline.
comments: 2026-03-02 | Ava Chen: Initial ticket created after pairing session with Diego. Design sketch attached in Confluence. Raised question about whether to treat partial tokens as idempotent units for resume semantics.
2026-03-03 | Diego Morales: Implemented prototype in PR #3184. Prototype exposes pullableStreamAdapter(options) that returns an AsyncGenerator. Needs stronger typings and cancellation tests.

2026-03-04 | Priya Kapoor (PM): Please ensure examples include a migration note for customers using existing stream adapters. Also flag UX: Console docs should include recommended retry budgets per model class.

2026-03-06 | Diego Morales: Ran stress tests. Observed leak when consumer cancels during backpressure spike — root cause: pending chunk promise not cleared from internal queue. Added fix by tracking inflight promises and draining on cancel.

2026-03-08 | Engineering review: LA team sign-off pending on retry token semantics. Proposed approach: retry token per-request that gates exactly-once consumption for idempotent model calls; non-idempotent flows default to fresh request and abort resume.
2026-03-10 | Ava Chen: Updated docs with two recipes: 'Browser Chat with Resume' and 'Node CLI stream consumer'. Requested review from DX and Docs before merge.
